texts.preamble: Muniyappa R vs Puttamma on 25 April, 2025 Kabc010196332020 C.R.P.67 Govt. of Karnataka Form No.9 (Civil) Title Sheet for Judgments in Suits (R.P.91) Title Sheet for Judgments in Suits
texts.facts: Present suit is filed on behalf of plaintiff against the defendants for Permanent Injunction and other reliefs. The description of the suit schedule property as mentioned in the plaint is as under: All that piece and parcel of the property bearing Sy.No.7/4B, No.31, Srinivagilu Main Road, Srinivagilu, Bengaluru, now coming under the jurisdiction of BBMP 4 O.S.No.5492/ 2020 Ward No.148 ( Old Ward No.68) measuring East-West- 60 feet and North-South- 70 feet, totally measuring 4200 square feet, consisting of 2400 squares Zinc Metal Sheet roofed structure thereon bounded on: East by : Apartment in Sy.No.8/2, West by : Road North by : Srinivagilu Main Road South by : Remaining portion of Sy.No.7/4B 2. The factual matrix in the nutshell is as under:- It is averred that, the plaintiff is a tenant of the property bearing Sy.No.7/4B, No.31 of Srinivagilu Main Road which is more fully described in the plaint schedule property, under defendants Nos.1 and 2 and said tenancy is governed by the Rental Agreement dtd.09.05.2020. The suit schedule property originally belonged to the father of defendant No.1, Sri Muniramaiah @ Moogappa who purchased the same vide registered Sale Deed dtd.15.04.1968. Pursuant to death of said Muniramaiah @ Moogappa, defendant No.1 i.e, his daughter has succeeded to the suit schedule property. 3 1st defendant and grandson of late Muniramaiah @ Moogappa. 5 O.S.No.5492/ 2020 3. It is further averred that, the plaintiff is carrying on eatery business under the name and style of "M/s Manish Mutton Dum Biryani" in the suit schedule property. Ever since he took the suit schedule property on lease on 09.05.2020, he is carrying on said business. Defendants Nos.1 and 2 being the landlords of said schedule premises/ suit schedule property, hired/ engaged defendants Nos.3 to 6 with a view to secure plaintiff's dispossession from the same. Defendants Nos.3 to 6 are notorious elements and 3rd defendant has a history of rowdy sheeter and defendants Nos.4 to 6 are his assistants. 4. It is further averred that, the plaintiff has obtained License from BBMP to run said eatery business under FSS Act, 2006 vide Registration No. 21220190000171 issued on 10.06.2020 by Food Safety Officer, Shanthinagar, BBMP, Bengaluru and said License is still valid. The only source of income for the livelihood of plaintiff and his family members is the income from 6 O.S.No.5492/ 2020 said eatery business. As to the workers engaged by the plaintiff, their source of livelihood is also depending on the business of the plaintiff in the suit schedule property. Muniyappa R vs Puttamma on 25 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19708066/ 4 5. It is further averred that, on 31.10.2020 at about 5.00 p.m., defendants Nos.1 and 2 entered the eatery of the plaintiff in the suit schedule property and behind them defendants No 3. to 6 along with some rowdy elements calculated to cause interference to the plaintiff carrying on his business in the suit schedule property and at that time there were customers in the same availing the services of plaintiff and after seeing them inside the suit schedule property, defendants Nos.3 to 6 walked out, so also miscreant elements brought by them also went along with them and defendants Nos.1 and 2 remained for sometime inside the suit schedule property. Defendants Nos.3 to 6 were watching from outside. After exit of the customers at about 6.00 to 6.30 p.m., defendants Nos.3 to 6 came inside along with said miscreant elements and picked up quarrel with the plaintiff and his old aged mother, aged about 80 years and tried to threaten them with dire consequences if the plaintiff does not vacate the premises on his 7 O.S.No.5492/ 2020 own and gave two weeks time to quit and deliver the possession, otherwise the plaintiff would have to face serious consequences. 6. It is further averred that, it is very difficult to find an alternative accommodation in the vicinity of the suit schedule property and further, getting the accommodation in the vicinity of the suit schedule property has become difficult due to Covid-19 Pandemic. In view of the above, he cannot oblige defendants Nos.1 and 2 to vacate suit schedule property and the continuation Muniyappa R vs Puttamma on 25 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19708066/ 5 of the plaintiff in the property to run the business therein stands exposed to the risk of dispossession by defendants Nos.1 and 2 by engaging defendants Nos.3 to 6. 7. Hence without any alternative, the plaintiff approached this Court seeking the relief of permanent injunction against the defendants. 10. In pursuance of service of suit summons, defendant Nos.1 to 6 appeared through their respective Counsels. Defendant Nos.3 to 6 have filed written statement and defendants Nos.1 and 2 have not filed any written statement. The suit schedule property bearing Sy.No.7/4 measuring to an extent of 0-6 guntas at Srinivagilu Village, belongs to Smt.Chinnamma and she acquired the same through registered Sale Deed on 16.04.1971. 13.
texts.arguments: The plaintiff has established good reputation in his business which is borne out by the view expressed by the customers and also in the vicinity of said premises, the plaintiff has earned good name for quality services provided by him. It is further averred that, deep apprehension has set in the mind of the plaintiff and his family members of possible dispossession from the suit schedule property and in such an event, the plaintiff would have to be on the street and further his family members would have to face problems for their survival. He finds himself in a very critical condition cornered by the defendants and he finds himself tensed up, unable to find out an alternative to the threat posed by the defendants herein. The 8 O.S.No.5492/ 2020 threat of dispossession posed by the defendants is very imminent and the apprehension of the plaintiff is that at any moment the defendants may throw him out using muscle power. In view of the above threat being imminent of dispossession of the plaintiff from the suit schedule property and further his business in said premises coming to standstill, cannot be ruled out and further to start afresh said business run by the plaintiff in the suit schedule property cannot be possible for the simple reason that he has to have all infrastructure facilities and to have the same, it takes considerable time and that depends on the availability of the suitable and adequate accommodation in the vicinity of said premises which stands ruled out. It is further averred that, the great threat posed to the plaintiff by the defendants is such and plaintiff's apprehension is that said threats could be materialized by the strategies worked out by the defendants and as such he is badly in need of an interim relief of injunction to enable him to run eatery business in the suit schedule property. 9 O.S.No.5492/ 2020 9. It is averred that, the cause of action arose within the jurisdiction of this Court since 31.10.2020 and thereafter when the defendants were persistently posing threats to the plaintiffs of their forcible dispossession from the suit schedule property. Hence, prayed for decreeing the suit by restraining the defendants, their agents and anybody whomsoever employed by them and acting at their behest, causing any interference to plaintiff's peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property and further to restrain defendants acting at their behest causing any interference to smooth functioning of eatery business run by the plaintiff in the suit schedule property and for such other reliefs. 11. In the written statement, defendants Nos.3 to 6 have denied all the averments of the plaint and contended that suit is not maintainable either in Law or on facts. There is no relationship of landlord and tenant in respect of suit schedule Muniyappa R vs Puttamma on 25 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19708066/ 7 property which totally belongs to Gundappa, Son of late 10 O.S.No.5492/ 2020 Chandrappa and the documents furnished are fraudulent in nature and attracting perjury and punishment from this Court. 12. It is further contended that, there is no cause of action for the suit. The suit schedule property as narrated in the Schedule and in the plaint does not exist as on the date of the suit , consequently the suit has to be dismissed. The allegations made in paras-8, 9, 12 all relate to past events, as a matter of fact, there exist no 'M/s. Manish Mutton Dum Biryani' as on the date of suit even till this date in the suit schedule property. The plaintiffs have vacated the adjoining premises long back and are falsely representing by obtaining bogus documents in relation to the Municipal Number in the suit schedule property. It is further contended that, Smt.Chinnamma expired on 10.04.1973 and after her demise her family members became legal heirs and Smt. Venkatamma, Muniraju, Smt.Chinnamma have released their right, title and interest in favour of 11 O.S.No.5492/ 2020 Sri.Gundappa, Son late Chandrappa of Srinivagilu Village. The plaintiff has purposely obtained bogus and fabricated documents, showing that the plaint schedule property is existing and has Muniyappa R vs Puttamma on 25 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19708066/ 8 wrongfully given the number of property belonging to Sri Gundappa, as such the suit is misconceived and has to be rejected and action for falsifying facts relating to the title of the property and perjury, action is to be taken in this regard. 14. It is further contended that the suit schedule property has been leased and it is in occupation of the tenant of Sri Gundappa. The plaintiff has maliciously suppressed the facts and purposely given the schedule and number of the property belonging to Gundappa by claiming tenancy rights on the basis of false, fabricated documents and is laying a false and frivolous claim. He has fraudulently obtained Corporation documents by giving the details of the property belonging to Gundappa with ulterior motive, as such the documents furnished such as Lease Deed, Hotel Records from BBMP are obtained by misrepresentation, undue influence and fraud and hence same cannot be looked into. 12 O.S.No.5492/ 2020 15. It is further contended that, the plaintiff is liable to be prosecuted for forgery and creating false evidence before the Court and for perjury, etc. The defendants reserve their rights, to file the additional written statement, if situation arises in this suit, consequently the suit for Permanent Injunction and any other relief needs to be dismissed / rejected with exemplary costs. Hence he is constrained to file the present suit seeking the relief of Permanent Injunction as prayed. 26 . In support of the plaintiff's case, he himself got examined as Pw.1 and filed his examination in chief affidavit in consonance with the plaint averments and has got marked totally 27 documents as Exs.P.1 to Ex.P.27, which include Rent Agreement, the License obtained from BBMP, Rent Receipts, 17 O.S.No.5492/ 2020 Certified copy of Sale Deed dt.15.04.1968, 15.04.1971, 16.06.1975, Encumbrance Certificate of the year 1968 to 2004, Balance sheet, profit and loss statement of the year 2019, 2020, 2021, copy of complaint given to Police Commissioner, DYSP and ACP, postal Acknowledgment, Police complaint given by Viveknagar police, Endorsement, Acknowledgment, statement of witnesses before police etc. 27. 31 . Here the defendants Nos.3 to 6 by filing detailed Written Statement have taken several contentions that, plaintiff 20 O.S.No.5492/ 2020 has created false documents with respect to the property of Gundappa and is making false claim in view of the suit property Muniyappa R vs Puttamma on 25 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/19708066/ 15 though he is not at all in possession and enjoyment of the same and thereby, he has committed fraud perjury etc,, for which he needs to be prosecuted and his claim is not maintainable etc. Hence adverse inference can be drawn against him in view of the Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 1999 SC 1441 in the case of Vidhyadhar V/s Manickrao, wherein it is clearly held that, person taking specific defence, if does not enter the witness box to substantiate their contention and tender for cross-examination an adverse inference can be drawn against him and it can be presumed that the defence taken by him is false. 32.
